processDefinition.name: Medical device field correction and recall
processDefinition.description: Illustrative U.S. medical device manufacturer recall lifecycle: detect a potential device issue, assess health risk and product status, select protective actions, coordinate regulatory obligations, trace affected distribution, notify consignees, complete corrections/removals, verify effectiveness, and seek regulatory termination when applicable. Based on FDA recall and 21 CFR 806 concepts, not an official workflow or legal advice. FDA owns recall classification and termination decisions; the company documents its assessments and requests. Workstreams may overlap in real events; sequence flows here document logical dependencies, not mandatory waiting periods. Public reference points: FDA Recalls, Corrections and Removals (https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/postmarket-requirements-devices/recalls-corrections-and-removals-devices); 21 CFR 806.10 and 806.20 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-806); FDA Product Recalls guidance (https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/product-recalls-including-removals-and-corrections). Regulatory requirements must be verified for the specific device and situation.

processElement.name: Potential device issue detected
processElement.description: A signal suggesting defective, mislabeled, unsafe or otherwise problematic marketed medical devices enters the manufacturer quality system.

processElement.name: Capture and triage issue
processElement.description: Capture evidence and determine urgency and scope of investigation. Establish accountable ownership and preserve records.

processElement.name: Investigate defect and health risk
processElement.description: Assess the technical issue, affected configurations and potential health hazard; distinguish established evidence from hypotheses.

processElement.name: Potential market action needed?
processElement.description: Firm decision: is market-facing correction or removal indicated after preliminary risk assessment? This is not an FDA recall classification.

processElement.name: Document no current field action
processElement.description: Record the evidence and basis for not initiating a market correction or removal at this time, plan surveillance and re-evaluation triggers.

processElement.name: No field action initiated
processElement.description: The investigation closes this path with ongoing surveillance and retained rationale; escalation remains possible if evidence changes.

processElement.name: Decide field strategy and obligations
processElement.description: Approve an appropriate firm action, outline recall strategy, and assess regulatory notifications without treating regulatory class as a company decision.

processElement.name: Identify products and consignees
processElement.description: Establish device scope, distribution reach, downstream recipients and inventory reconciliation.

processElement.name: Notify and support affected parties
processElement.description: Issue approved instructions, manage consignee responses, and arrange patient/clinical and public communication as appropriate.

processElement.name: Perform field correction or removal
processElement.description: Execute appropriate on-site correction, replacement, removal or return actions and preserve unit-level evidence.

processElement.name: Verify recall effectiveness
processElement.description: Check whether intended recipients received communications and took required action; address unresolved gaps.

processElement.name: Is recall action adequately effective?
processElement.description: Internal review of verified evidence and remaining gaps; any FDA determination of termination is separate.

processElement.name: Escalate unresolved gaps
processElement.description: Plan targeted outreach, revised communications, or further field work for missing units or incomplete actions; retain an escalation record.

processElement.name: Reconcile and pursue closure
processElement.description: Reconcile outcomes, coordinate any applicable FDA termination request, and address root causes and sustained controls.

processElement.name: Recall case completed
processElement.description: Firm documentation and relevant agency communication are complete; if FDA-regulated recall, the agency alone determines formal termination.

processElement.name: Begin capture and triage issue
processElement.description: A complaint, trend, regulatory observation or other signal is received.

processElement.name: Complete capture and triage issue
processElement.description: A controlled issue file, assigned owner and preservation actions are available.

processElement.name: Register and date the issue
processElement.description: Record source, discovery timing, device identifiers, observed failure, clinical outcomes, and supporting attachments.

processElement.name: Evaluate immediate safety escalation
processElement.description: Identify credible serious harm and urgent protective communications. Do not wait for full root-cause confirmation before appropriate escalation.

processElement.name: Is immediate escalation warranted?
processElement.description: Determine whether urgent risk and safety escalation are required; this is an internal triage criterion.

processElement.name: Mobilize emergency response contacts
processElement.description: Notify medical, regulatory, legal and company incident contacts to assess immediate protections and reporting duties.

processElement.name: Assign recall coordinator and preserve evidence
processElement.description: Assign case ownership, preserve complaint records and relevant device traceability data; establish a controlled record.

processElement.name: Define initial investigation objectives
processElement.description: Specify suspected device families, key unanswered questions and the initial technical and clinical investigation boundaries.

processElement.name: Begin investigate defect and health risk
processElement.description: Issue evidence and a bounded investigation plan are available.

processElement.name: Complete investigate defect and health risk
processElement.description: The technical findings, device scope and health hazard evaluation are documented.

processElement.name: Gather device and production history
processElement.description: Collect design history, manufacturing deviations, service logs, software changes and complaint trends for suspect devices.

processElement.name: Investigate and replicate observed failure
processElement.description: Test the problem where feasible, document uncertainty, and distinguish a confirmed defect from plausible mechanisms.

processElement.name: Establish preliminary affected product scope
processElement.description: Map failure mechanisms to lots, serials, software configurations, manufacturing periods and distribution evidence.

processElement.name: Is affected scope sufficiently bounded?
processElement.description: Decide whether additional evidence is necessary to bound the affected device population safely.

processElement.name: Expand sampling and worst-case boundary
processElement.description: Include potentially affected configurations while investigating unknown boundary conditions; document assumptions and follow-up evidence.

processElement.name: Perform clinical health hazard evaluation
processElement.description: Assess severity, probability, exposure and patient risks in a documented clinical/quality review; this does not assign FDA recall classification.

processElement.name: Integrate defect, scope and clinical findings
processElement.description: Reconcile hazard evaluation with affected-device scope, uncertainties, and potential protective options.

processElement.name: Approve initial investigation conclusions
processElement.description: Document who reviewed evidence, disagreements and confidence levels; escalate unresolved patient-protection concerns.

processElement.name: Begin perform clinical health hazard evaluation
processElement.description: The suspected failure and preliminary device scope are available.

processElement.name: Complete perform clinical health hazard evaluation
processElement.description: A clinical hazard assessment with uncertainties and source evidence is approved.

processElement.name: Characterize intended and foreseeable use
processElement.description: Identify intended use, clinical setting, patient vulnerabilities, modes of exposure and alternative therapies.

processElement.name: Review adverse events and clinical evidence
processElement.description: Assess known injuries, near misses, complaints, field reports and relevant medical literature without presuming causality.

processElement.name: Assess severity and probability
processElement.description: Document possible adverse health consequences, likelihood and uncertainty; consider both routine and foreseeable misuse scenarios.

processElement.name: Review high-risk populations and settings
processElement.description: Consider pediatric, critical-care, home-use and implanted-device contexts where applicable; record clinical constraints.

processElement.name: Assess interim patient risk mitigations
processElement.description: Evaluate stop-use advice, inspection, close monitoring, alternative devices and whether continued use may be clinically necessary.

processElement.name: Sign health hazard assessment
processElement.description: Obtain medical and quality review, record assumptions, uncertainty, and triggers for re-evaluation if evidence changes.

processElement.name: Begin decide field strategy and obligations
processElement.description: Initial firm action decision and health hazard evidence are available.

processElement.name: Complete decide field strategy and obligations
processElement.description: Firm action strategy, regulatory plan and resourcing are documented.

processElement.name: Convene interdisciplinary recall decision team
processElement.description: Review evidence, define accountable owner, affected markets and decision authority. Decisions remain firm actions subject to regulator review.

processElement.name: Choose correction, removal or other measure
processElement.description: Specify practical protective measures: stop-use, repair, software update, replacement, retrieval or other appropriate action.

processElement.name: Define recall depth and effectiveness approach
processElement.description: Propose direct/downstream consignee reach, risk-tailored effectiveness checks and contingencies for unknown distribution.

processElement.name: Plan continuity of essential care and supply
processElement.description: Assess substitute devices, access constraints and clinical risks from abrupt withdrawal; coordinate safe alternatives.

processElement.name: Assess regulatory obligations and engage FDA
processElement.description: Evaluate FDA reporting and recordkeeping requirements, share the firm action plan and record agency feedback; FDA retains classification authority.

processElement.name: Authorize firm recall action plan
processElement.description: Approve action plan, accountabilities and resource allocation, track open regulatory questions and implementation contingencies.

processElement.name: Release controlled field-action instructions
processElement.description: Provide approved technical work instructions and quality acceptance criteria to field teams without delaying urgent protection unnecessarily.

processElement.name: Begin assess regulatory obligations and engage fda
processElement.description: The proposed correction/removal and scope are known.

processElement.name: Complete assess regulatory obligations and engage fda
processElement.description: The regulatory analysis, applicable reports and communications are recorded.

processElement.name: Identify affected jurisdictions and obligations
processElement.description: Identify U.S. regulatory scope and coordinate separate market requirements for any other countries; no assumption of identical rules.

processElement.name: Assess 21 CFR 806 reporting criteria
processElement.description: Determine whether the initiated correction or removal meets 21 CFR 806.10 reporting criteria or an applicable exception; preserve documented rationale.

processElement.name: Is a Part 806 report required?
processElement.description: Assessment of reporting duty; a required 806.10 report is generally due within 10 working days after initiating the correction/removal, subject to regulatory exceptions.

processElement.name: Prepare and submit required FDA report
processElement.description: Submit 21 CFR 806.10 information within the applicable time period if required; coordinate other required reports without assuming one filing substitutes for another.

processElement.name: Record nonreporting basis and required records
processElement.description: If no 806.10 report is due, document the analysis and retain correction/removal records as required by 21 CFR 806.20 where applicable.

processElement.name: Coordinate FDA recall contact and strategy review
processElement.description: Communicate with FDA recall coordinator as applicable, supply product, distribution, risk and strategy information, and log feedback.

processElement.name: Record FDA classification when issued
processElement.description: Track whether FDA classifies the action as Class I, II or III; record FDA determination rather than assigning an internal class.

processElement.name: Begin identify products and consignees
processElement.description: Initial affected product identity is available.

processElement.name: Complete identify products and consignees
processElement.description: A controlled account tree and reconciliation baseline are issued.

processElement.name: Extract shipment and serial histories
processElement.description: Compile factory release, shipments, RMA, consignment and service records using consistent product identifiers.

processElement.name: Reconcile manufactured and released units
processElement.description: Separate manufactured, scrapped, in-house and released volumes; document unexplained differences and suspected gaps.

processElement.name: Map direct accounts and contact owners
processElement.description: Identify distributors, clinical sites and direct purchasers, with contact channels and responsible follow-up owners.

processElement.name: Trace downstream distribution where necessary
processElement.description: Seek distributor and transfer records to determine whether affected devices reached additional facilities or users.

processElement.name: Are distribution records complete enough?
processElement.description: Assess whether all expected units and reachable recipients have an accountable path or documented uncertainty.

processElement.name: Investigate unaccounted units and contacts
processElement.description: Escalate unidentified destinations, incomplete identifiers and downstream gaps; use conservative outreach when justified.

processElement.name: Approve controlled distribution baseline
processElement.description: Issue versioned affected-device and consignee inventory, assign unresolved items and establish update process for late discoveries.

processElement.name: Begin notify and support affected parties
processElement.description: The recall strategy and consignee baseline are available.

processElement.name: Complete notify and support affected parties
processElement.description: Customers receive controlled instructions and a documented outreach/response plan.

processElement.name: Draft consignee recall communications
processElement.description: State affected product identification, reason for action, hazards, immediate steps, completion requirements and how to respond.

processElement.name: Approve clinically and legally accurate wording
processElement.description: Check plain-language instructions, device traceability, contact details, escalation and consistency with regulatory requirements.

processElement.name: Distribute notifications to all in-scope consignees
processElement.description: Send tracked communications according to the recall depth, including distributors and direct clinical sites.

processElement.name: Record responses and action commitments
processElement.description: Log acknowledgement, whether further distribution occurred, device status, intended action and responder details.

processElement.name: Are critical responses outstanding?
processElement.description: Check whether unresponsive recipients or missing downstream contacts require urgent additional outreach.

processElement.name: Escalate nonresponders and downstream alerts
processElement.description: Use alternative contact methods and distributor escalation; revise instructions if effectiveness feedback exposes ambiguity.

processElement.name: Coordinate patient and public safety communications
processElement.description: Coordinate any clinically appropriate patient notices, clinician advice and public warnings under the agreed recall strategy.

processElement.name: Publish and maintain contact status
processElement.description: Maintain outreach status, updated consignee lists and communication version history for subsequent effectiveness checks.

processElement.name: Begin coordinate patient and public safety communications
processElement.description: Recall strategy and preliminary communications are approved.

processElement.name: Complete coordinate patient and public safety communications
processElement.description: Clinician/patient/public communication decisions and evidence are recorded.

processElement.name: Is a broader public warning indicated?
processElement.description: Determine whether the recall strategy calls for public communication, considering health risk and affected population.

processElement.name: Prepare and approve public / clinician notice
processElement.description: Coordinate public warnings and clinician instructions with regulatory, clinical and communications stakeholders as appropriate.

processElement.name: Document communication scope decision
processElement.description: Document why public communications are not part of the present strategy and what evidence would cause reconsideration.

processElement.name: Prepare clinically appropriate continuity guidance
processElement.description: Describe how clinicians should assess continued device use, substitutes, monitoring and high-risk patient concerns.

processElement.name: Distribute through appropriate clinical channels
processElement.description: Coordinate dissemination through treating facilities or other appropriate channels without assuming manufacturer access to patient identity.

processElement.name: Begin perform field correction or removal
processElement.description: Approved affected-device scope and field instructions are available.

processElement.name: Complete perform field correction or removal
processElement.description: Corrected, returned and unresolved device units are documented.

processElement.name: Create unit-level work and site plan
processElement.description: Match affected serials to sites, prioritize clinical risk and arrange qualified personnel and equipment.

processElement.name: Verify device identity and status on site
processElement.description: Confirm product identifiers, firmware and recall eligibility before intervention; record unknown or missing units.

processElement.name: Is in-place correction appropriate?
processElement.description: Choose correction at point of use versus controlled return/removal based on approved technical and clinical criteria.

processElement.name: Perform approved correction or update
processElement.description: Inspect, replace component, adjust setting or update software according to controlled work instructions.

processElement.name: Test and sign corrected device acceptance
processElement.description: Run specified post-correction tests, capture results and return-to-use authorization with qualified oversight.

processElement.name: Remove, return and disposition devices
processElement.description: Coordinate safe removal, shipping, quarantine, disposition and reconciliation when correction in place is unsuitable.

processElement.name: Reconcile field actions to affected serials
processElement.description: Connect work order evidence, returned inventory, unresolved cases and customer confirmations to the affected device list.

processElement.name: Approve completion and exception status
processElement.description: Document accepted corrections, outstanding units, care continuity measures and limitations on declaring completion.

processElement.name: Begin remove, return and disposition devices
processElement.description: A device has been assigned for removal or return.

processElement.name: Complete remove, return and disposition devices
processElement.description: Dispositions and associated custody records are reconciled.

processElement.name: Plan safe withdrawal and replacement
processElement.description: Coordinate patient safety, substitutes, transport limitations and facility handoff for devices to be removed.

processElement.name: Identify, isolate and package device
processElement.description: Record identifiers, disable use as appropriate, package safely and create controlled return instructions.

processElement.name: Track transport and chain of custody
processElement.description: Record shipper, movement dates, custody transfers, exceptions and delivery confirmations.

processElement.name: Receive and quarantine returned product
processElement.description: Verify serials and condition, separate affected units from available inventory and document deviations.

processElement.name: Is rework permitted under the plan?
processElement.description: Select approved rework versus disposal, using documented technical and quality criteria.

processElement.name: Apply validated rework process
processElement.description: Perform approved remediation, testing, re-labeling or other disposition with required quality controls.

processElement.name: Destroy or otherwise dispose of affected device
processElement.description: Document controlled destruction or other approved disposition and maintain traceability to affected serials.

processElement.name: Reconcile logistics ledger
processElement.description: Compare returns, actions, disposal evidence and expected quantities; flag any missing items.

processElement.name: Begin verify recall effectiveness
processElement.description: Communication and field action records are available.

processElement.name: Complete verify recall effectiveness
processElement.description: Validated effectiveness evidence and outstanding follow-up are captured.

processElement.name: Approve effectiveness check methodology
processElement.description: Select scope, response criteria, risk-informed sample and ways to verify action rather than notification delivery alone.

processElement.name: Contact consignees and test completion
processElement.description: Verify receipt of recall notice and action taken; document contact method, responses and evidence supporting claims.

processElement.name: Verify downstream and transferred products
processElement.description: Determine whether further distribution occurred and whether secondary recipients were informed and acted.

processElement.name: Compare responses with serial-level records
processElement.description: Reconcile contact replies with field work, product disposition, distributions and unresolved exceptions.

processElement.name: Did effectiveness checks reveal gaps?
processElement.description: Distinguish evidence of completed action from email reads or claimed acknowledgement; use findings to drive remediation.

processElement.name: Plan tailored corrective follow-up
processElement.description: Initiate alternate contact methods, clarification notices, supplemental field service or deeper downstream tracing.

processElement.name: Approve effectiveness assessment
processElement.description: Document results, limitations, selected follow-up and whether sufficient evidence is present for closure consideration.

processElement.name: Begin reconcile and pursue closure
processElement.description: Effectiveness assessment indicates the firm can consider closure.

processElement.name: Complete reconcile and pursue closure
processElement.description: Firm closeout, regulatory follow-up and prevention work are recorded.

processElement.name: Reconcile quantities and disposition evidence
processElement.description: Compare scope, distribution, contacts, actions, returns, outstanding cases and risk decisions; flag exceptions.

processElement.name: Are material closure gaps resolved?
processElement.description: Decide whether more work is required before internal closeout or termination materials; FDA termination is not decided here.

processElement.name: Assign unresolved recall closure issues
processElement.description: Reopen targeted investigations, service visits or communications as needed; record ongoing exceptions.

processElement.name: Prepare firm completion and any termination request
processElement.description: Submit status evidence to FDA as applicable and respond to agency questions; firm requests do not constitute FDA termination.

processElement.name: Record FDA oversight and termination status
processElement.description: Record official agency communication, including classification or termination when issued; track pending status separately.

processElement.name: Investigate causes and prevent recurrence
processElement.description: Connect recall observations to root-cause analysis, quality system action, verification, training and continued monitoring.

processElement.name: Archive the controlled recall record
processElement.description: Preserve approvals, data versions, customer communications, disposition records, safety assessments and closure rationale per requirements.

processElement.name: Begin investigate causes and prevent recurrence
processElement.description: Recall findings and unresolved systemic issues are available.

processElement.name: Complete investigate causes and prevent recurrence
processElement.description: Corrective/preventive actions and monitoring are assigned with evidence.

processElement.name: Investigate systemic root causes
processElement.description: Identify causes and contributing quality-system failures, including supplier, design, training and surveillance factors.

processElement.name: Define corrective and preventive actions
processElement.description: Assign accountable owners, due dates, verification criteria and controls appropriate to root causes and risk.

processElement.name: Implement design or process changes
processElement.description: Apply document-controlled changes and evaluate any newly created risks or regulatory obligations.

processElement.name: Verify and validate changed controls
processElement.description: Perform verification or validation appropriate to the change, record discrepancies and manage implementation evidence.

processElement.name: Do CAPA controls pass acceptance criteria?
processElement.description: Assess documented effectiveness evidence, not simply closure of action tickets.

processElement.name: Revise inadequate corrective actions
processElement.description: Revisit root cause, expand containment and amend action plan after failed verification or renewed signals.

processElement.name: Establish recurrence surveillance and lessons learned
processElement.description: Plan complaint trending, manufacturing monitoring, governance review and lessons learned across functions.

performerDefinition.name: Quality assurance / recall coordinator
performerDefinition.description: Leads internal recall coordination, records decisions and evidence, and tracks action completeness.

performerDefinition.name: Complaint handling team
performerDefinition.description: Collects complaints, incident observations and follow-up evidence from field sources.

performerDefinition.name: Product engineering
performerDefinition.description: Investigates device faults, affected configurations and correction feasibility.

performerDefinition.name: Clinical safety / medical officer
performerDefinition.description: Evaluates potential clinical harms, exposure routes and patient safety implications.

performerDefinition.name: Regulatory affairs
performerDefinition.description: Assesses reporting requirements and coordinates communications and submissions to regulators.

performerDefinition.name: Legal / compliance counsel
performerDefinition.description: Advises on jurisdictional obligations, record preservation and communication approvals.

performerDefinition.name: Recall decision authority
performerDefinition.description: Authorizes resources and firm action within the organization; does not make FDA classification decisions.

performerDefinition.name: Manufacturing operations
performerDefinition.description: Identifies lots and inventories and supports field correction or replacement.

performerDefinition.name: Supply chain / inventory
performerDefinition.description: Maps shipped units, warehouses and disposition of available stock.

performerDefinition.name: Distributor liaison
performerDefinition.description: Coordinates downstream account tracing and consignee responses.

performerDefinition.name: Customer communications
performerDefinition.description: Prepares notices, sends instructions and follows up on missing acknowledgments.

performerDefinition.name: Field service engineer
performerDefinition.description: Repairs, inspects, replaces or removes affected devices at points of use.

performerDefinition.name: Healthcare facility contact
performerDefinition.description: Local receiving contact who identifies affected devices and coordinates appropriate site action.

performerDefinition.name: Information systems / traceability analyst
performerDefinition.description: Extracts product identifiers and shipments, reconciles files and maintains traceability evidence.

performerDefinition.name: Reverse logistics coordinator
performerDefinition.description: Coordinates shipping, controlled returns, quarantine and disposition evidence.

performerDefinition.name: Effectiveness check auditor
performerDefinition.description: Independently tests whether notified consignees received and followed instructions.

performerDefinition.name: CAPA / quality systems owner
performerDefinition.description: Connects recall findings to corrective and preventive action and long-term monitoring.

performerDefinition.name: Public communications
performerDefinition.description: Supports public notices when required by the strategy and appropriate authorities.

performerDefinition.name: FDA recall coordinator (external)
performerDefinition.description: External authority for recall review, classification, oversight and termination; represented as stakeholder, not firm-controlled execution.

performerDefinition.name: Clinical provider / patient liaison
performerDefinition.description: Coordinates appropriate patient-facing information through qualified clinical channels.

processDataItem.name: Issue signal / complaint record
processDataItem.description: Initial complaint, incident report, trend signal or external alert with provenance and dates.

processDataItem.name: Complaint investigation file
processDataItem.description: Verified observations, investigation contacts, device history and evidence relevant to initial triage.

processDataItem.name: Device identification and UDI mapping
processDataItem.description: Model, product code, lot, serial, UDI, software versions and other affected-product identifiers.

processDataItem.name: Failure analysis findings
processDataItem.description: Engineering hypotheses, testing results, confirmed defects and their boundaries.

processDataItem.name: Patient and use exposure profile
processDataItem.description: Affected patient populations, likely usage, frequency and extent of exposure.

processDataItem.name: Health hazard assessment
processDataItem.description: Documented clinical severity, probability, reversibility, uncertainties and medical evaluation.

processDataItem.name: Affected product scope determination
processDataItem.description: Evidence-backed included/excluded lots, configurations, dates and rationale.

processDataItem.name: Firm action determination
processDataItem.description: Internal documented reasoning on whether and how to correct, remove or take another action.

processDataItem.name: Recall strategy
processDataItem.description: Planned recall depth, communications, corrections/removals, public warning considerations and effectiveness checks.

processDataItem.name: Regulatory obligation assessment
processDataItem.description: Country-specific analysis of 21 CFR 806 and other reporting/notification obligations.

processDataItem.name: FDA correction/removal report or rationale
processDataItem.description: Where required, a report under 21 CFR 806.10; otherwise documented non-reporting basis and applicable records.

processDataItem.name: FDA communications and response log
processDataItem.description: Contacts, submissions, agency feedback, classification communications and other correspondence.

processDataItem.name: FDA recall classification record
processDataItem.description: Agency-issued Class I, II or III determination when applicable; company does not determine FDA class.

processDataItem.name: Sales, shipping and distribution ledger
processDataItem.description: Manufacturer direct shipment transactions, dates, quantities, parties and downstream references.

processDataItem.name: Consignee contact and distribution tree
processDataItem.description: Direct and downstream recipients, destinations, contact owners and follow-up statuses.

processDataItem.name: Inventory reconciliation
processDataItem.description: Quantities manufactured, released, shipped, in stock, on hold, returned, corrected or unaccounted.

processDataItem.name: Customer recall notification package
processDataItem.description: Approved notice, device identification, risks, stop-use/correction instructions and acknowledgement methods.

processDataItem.name: Notification acknowledgement and escalation log
processDataItem.description: Consignee response, receipt, action claims, nonresponses, contact attempts and escalations.

processDataItem.name: Public / clinician safety communication
processDataItem.description: Public warning or clinician/patient-facing content, with approval and dissemination evidence when appropriate.

processDataItem.name: Field execution work order
processDataItem.description: Device-specific inspection, repair, software correction, removal or replacement instructions.

processDataItem.name: Field correction verification record
processDataItem.description: Serial-level action performed, technician, date, test results and acceptance evidence.

processDataItem.name: Return and disposition ledger
processDataItem.description: Shipment tracking, chain of custody, quarantine, scrapping/rework and final disposition.

processDataItem.name: Care continuity and substitute supply plan
processDataItem.description: Constraints, substitute devices and steps to minimize interruption of essential care.

processDataItem.name: Effectiveness check protocol
processDataItem.description: Risk-informed sample, contact method, response criteria, documentation and follow-up plan.

processDataItem.name: Effectiveness check results
processDataItem.description: Evidence of notification receipt, corrective actions taken and unresolved or ineffective responses.

processDataItem.name: Unresolved consignee / action gap register
processDataItem.description: Nonresponses, missing devices, unsafe continued use and corrective follow-up status.

processDataItem.name: Final recall reconciliation
processDataItem.description: Evidence tying affected units, consignees, required action, exceptions and final status together.

processDataItem.name: Firm closure and termination dossier
processDataItem.description: Internal closure rationale, submitted termination materials and FDA termination status if applicable.

processDataItem.name: CAPA investigation and action plan
processDataItem.description: Root causes, containment, systemic corrective and preventive actions and owners.

processDataItem.name: Design and production change evidence
processDataItem.description: Validated design changes, manufacturing controls, labeling and verification records.

processDataItem.name: Lessons learned and monitoring plan
processDataItem.description: Post-event governance, training, surveillance triggers, and sustained effectiveness monitoring.

processDataItem.name: Records retention / legal hold register
processDataItem.description: Relevant documents, preservation directions, access and applicable retention obligations.

processOpenQuestion.description: What written criteria and escalation authority distinguish a field correction/removal from an issue handled through monitoring or a non-recall measure?
Which workstreams may start before upstream analysis is complete, especially urgent patient protection and regulatory notification?
Which complaint patterns or clinical events mandate immediate escalation, including after-hours contacts?
How should unknown, untracked or mixed-version devices be included in the provisional affected population?
Who determines patient-specific advice when immediate removal creates risk from loss of essential treatment?
Who can authorize an urgent action outside routine recall committee hours?
Who records the exact initiation date for each field action and monitors the applicable 10-working-day deadline?
Are there separate medical device reporting or international vigilance duties triggered by the same event?
What evidence is required when distributor downstream records cannot be obtained?
How will communications reach patients or users when the manufacturer only knows institutional consignees?
Who decides when to issue a public warning, and which agency coordination or legal review applies?
What acceptance evidence is necessary for a remote software correction versus on-site physical service?
What counts as verified action for remote sites where direct inspection is impractical?
How is effectiveness-check depth and sampling selected, reviewed, and adapted to the risk?
Who distinguishes internal firm completion from formal FDA termination and how is pending agency status displayed?
What evidence and monitoring interval will demonstrate that the underlying failure mode is controlled?
Who owns versioning of the affected serial list after field work has already begun?
Which languages and accessible formats are needed for different markets and clinical settings?
How should units that were shipped but never installed be verified and closed?
How should patient privacy be protected while assessing clinical exposure?
What activities can run concurrently, and what evidence must exist before each can be considered complete?
